bounded_local_followup.purpose: A separate small-model implementation pilot for short evidence units; not a replacement for the frozen 8B full-history protocol or paper-level extraction quality evidence.
steps: Resolve an immutable official Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-GGUF repository commit, selected quantized file, file size, license, and SHA-256 from primary metadata. Keep the existing 8B configuration unchanged.

Resolve a CPU llama.cpp or llama-cpp-python runtime to an immutable release/commit and artifact hash in a workspace-only environment. Verify architecture support and local execution before any extraction.

Use one batch, at most 4 CPU threads, a 2048-token context, at most 128 generated tokens, and a 60-second one-request smoke timeout. Reject overlong inputs rather than truncating them. Select a weight file no larger than 1 GiB.

Require measured process peak resident memory below 1.5 GiB for the smoke request, zero swap-based capacity assumptions, and an explicit lower limit if the runtime reveals one. Fail safely on any resource error. This is a target budget, not verified fit.

Preserve raw prompt/template/token IDs, model/runtime asset hashes, raw output and generated token IDs when exposed, stop reason, parse outcome, elapsed time and measured peak memory. No hidden retries or output repair.

Before a scoring pilot, verify that the chosen runtime exposes comparable token log probabilities, then freeze a source-only candidate/scoring protocol with no development expectations or QA answers in model inputs.
Run identical cached candidates and scores through all decoder variants. Label this small-model protocol separately and record all prompt/context differences from the 8B protocol.
bounded_local_followup.scientific_limit: A successful short CPU smoke run establishes transport/runtime only. It does not establish adequate candidate recall, scoring calibration, correction understanding, generalization, or a joint-inference advantage.

limits: Not a pinned backend result or a replacement for the frozen 8B protocol.
Use a fresh agent context containing eligible source text, frozen task instructions and allowed schema only.
Exclude prior annotations, development expectations, questions and gold from extraction/scoring inputs.
Save exact task text, source hashes, raw output and any validation failures.
Share a single candidate/score cache across decoder variants and describe scores as unversioned conversational judgments.
Do not claim model reproducibility, calibration, independent human annotation, held-out accuracy or paper-level algorithmic superiority.
